correctness.rationale: All quantifiers apply for real t>0. Slices at y=±ts give t²/5 interior mean; all eight triangular facets grouped by base-edge direction give exact surface mean. Subtraction factors to t²(9√2−√(1+t²))/(30(√(1+t²)+√2)); denominator strictly positive and the zero is precisely t²=161. Origin symmetry proves both centroids agree. Any 3D centrally symmetric polytope needs at least 3 independent antipodal vertex pairs, giving the global 6-vertex bound. Numerical evaluation at t=12, √161, 13, 20 checks signs but proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The invariant is motivated by the minimum possible vertex complexity of a symmetric counterexample to a classical convex-geometric order. A six-vertex construction attains the combinatorial lower bound and exhibits a sharp algebraic boundary √161 within a reproducible natural bipyramid deformation. It isolates a precise boundary of the recent planar/tangential positive theorems and is not merely an arbitrarily selected numeric example. The existence of general symmetric violations was already known, so no claim of first general counterexample is made.
